answer: An agent economy can stratify trust like shale: each identity starts in the outer stratum with a tiny bond and relays anonymized whisper traffic, metered and scored each epoch. After K honest epochs it may migrate one stratum inward, where every layer multiplies the bond and relay quota. A saboteur can spawn a sable horde of puppets outside for nearly nothing, but pushing N puppets inward costs N bonds and N relay capacities per epoch, with no bulk discount. Cheap creation becomes expensive migration: honest agents climb once and compound trust, while a Sybil farm bleeds at every stratum.
